candidates.exact_span: The annual whole sludge application rate for the sewage sludge that does not cause any of the cumulative pollutant loading rates in Table 2 above to be exceeded, unless the pollutant concentrations in Table 3 found in Element I, Section III below are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the Table 2 cumulative loading-rate framework or the Table 3 concentration criteria governs depends on how 'met' and 'exceeded' are interpreted and on cross-references not present in this segment; that choice changes which numeric limits are enforceable (A), what pollutant monitoring must support the applicable pathway (B), and how absent or borderline results are classified when the operative limit framework is unclear (C).

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 3 found in Element I, Section III and the applicable pollutant concentration criteria (mg/Kg), or the applicable cumulative pollutant loading rate and the applicable cumulative pollutant loading rate limit (kg/ha) listed in Table 2 above.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This recordkeeping clause ties required documentation to either concentration criteria or cumulative loading-rate limits; interpreting whether 'or' is elective, mutually exclusive, or condition-dependent changes which numeric standards apply for compliance comparison (A), which measurements must have been obtained and retained (B), and whether missing records reflect a no-data state, unmet monitoring duty, or unresolved applicability (C).

candidates.exact_span: The person who prepares bulk sewage sludge or a sewage sludge material shall develop the following information and shall retain the information for five years.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The scope of 'develop' and the five-year retention duty define an evidentiary monitoring/recordkeeping obligation; different readings of who must develop the information and when the duty attaches change which monitoring requirements are treated as applicable (B) and whether absent data is a documented no-data state versus inadequate evidence of required monitoring (C).

candidates.exact_span: If the permittee supplies the sludge to another person who land applies the sludge, the permittee shall notify the land applier of the requirements for recordkeeping found in 40 CFR 503.17 for persons who land apply.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability hinges on whether sludge was supplied to a land applier and whether notification satisfied the cross-reference to 40 CFR 503.17; that affects which party's monitoring and recordkeeping obligations are operative (B) and how missing evidence is attributed when preparation, transfer, and land application are split among persons (C).

candidates.exact_span: Any change shall include any planned physical alterations or additions to the permitted treatment works, changes in the permittee's sludge use or disposal practice, and also alterations, additions, or deletions of disposal sites. These changes may justify the application of permit conditions that are different from or absent in the existing permit, including notification of additional disposal sites not reported during the permit application process or absent in the existing permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: What counts as a covered 'change' and whether different permit conditions are triggered determines which monitoring requirements tied to disposal sites or sludge practices are in force during Federal FY2025; alternative interpretations of these change categories would change evaluated monitoring-obligation rows and unresolved applicability cases (B).

candidates.exact_span: the permittee shall within 30 days after notification by the State Historical Commission that a specific sludge disposal/use area will adversely affect a National Historic Site, cease use of such area.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and when a site is subject to mandatory cessation affects whether later missing monitoring evidence should be classified as a documented no-application/no-discharge period, a conditional monitoring non-requirement, or an unresolved gap; the timing and triggering of 'cease use' therefore changes missing-evidence semantics (C).
